rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a can or metal container, especially when naming its contents.

example.english: This can of soda is mine.
example.jyutping: nei1 gun3 hei3 seoi2 hai6 ngo5 ge3

rows.note: Use 可以 as the all-purpose choice for general ability, permission, and possibility.

example.english: We can finish work early today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 ho2 ji5 zou2 di1 sau1 gung1

rows.note: Use 得 for a short, casual sense of being able, allowed, or feasible, especially in 得唔得 questions.

example.english: Can we do it this way?
example.jyutping: gam2 joeng2 zou6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3

rows.note: Use 識得 for knowing how to do something, including the know-how slice of general ability.

example.jyutping: ngo5 sik1 dak1 zing2 ni1 mei6 sung3

rows.note: Use 可唔可以 + V to make a typically polite request.

example.english: Can you lend me a pen?
example.jyutping: ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 ze3 zi1 bat1 bei2 ngo5

rows.note: Use this specifically for a container used to water plants rather than an ordinary can.

example.english: Remember to take the watering can outside to water the plants.
example.traditional: 記得攞淋花壺出去淋花。
example.jyutping: gei3 dak1 lo2 lam4 faa1 wu2 ceot1 heoi3 lam4 faa1
